target_customer: Affluent consumers, travelers, investors and professionals in Latin America who want dollar and euro balances, a card and investing
problem: People in Latin American countries with weak local currencies and limited access to dollar accounts need a way to hold, spend, receive and send dollars at real market rates.
business_model: Consumer and business fintech: FX spread, card interchange, transfer fees and earnings products

founders.name: Fernando Terres
founders.background_notes: Latamlist (Sept 2022) says all three founders are former Revolut employees; YC launch post says the three spent a couple of years at Revolut.

founders.name: Zach Garman
previous_startups: Ethereum-based digital identity product (co-founded, name not given)

founders.name: Alvaro Correa
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page; Revolut background per Latamlist.

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard fintech app built on licensed partners and stablecoin rails; hard parts are compliance, banking partners and FX liquidity rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Licenses, bank partnerships and user trust help, but Wise, Revolut and local crypto exchanges can offer similar dollar accounts.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or acquiring it; a 2026 article lists Revolut, Wise, Payoneer, GrabrFi, Global66 and Wenia as rivals.

market_need_then: High demand for dollar access in Latin America due to currency instability; the seed announcement described beta users swapping pesos to USDC and a dollar card with cashback.

branding.name_origin: DolarApp literally meant dollar app in Spanish; the company says the name no longer fit its broader offering and renamed to ARQ in March 2026.
branding.domain_note: Used dolarapp.com; now arqfinance.com. No acquisition story found.

identity.visual_style: Premium fintech positioning toward affluent users

rebrands.why: Company help center says the old name was too narrow for a wider product range including spending, investing and credit

branding.community_and_virality: Company claims about 2 million users and 4.6 to 4.7 app ratings; testimonials on site. No evidence of merch or fan culture found.

brand_strength.rationale: DolarApp was clear and descriptive in the Spanish-speaking market and helped adoption; the rebrand to ARQ in 2026 came with a $70M round, so the new brand's strength is untested.

outcome_analysis: DolarApp raised a $5M seed from YC and Kaszek in September 2022, grew to a claimed 2 million users across Latin America, and raised $70M in March 2026 led by Sequoia and Founders Fund while rebranding to ARQ. Success rests on strong demand for dollar access, ex-Revolut founders, and stablecoin rails; the risks are regulatory dependence and rivals like Wise, Revolut and Bitso.
notes: Competitors: no dated source near the 2021 batch found; the La Republica competitor list is from 2026 so not used. The March 2026 round is labeled Series A by Seedtable and Series B by Briter, so stage is other. Company site lists Brevan Howard as an investor (not tied to a round).
